Install a Key Expansion Module on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones
## Objective
The Cisco IP Phone 8800 Key Expansion Module (KEM) expands the capabilities of your IP Phone, providing it with additional physical keys that can be programmed with additional directory numbers, speed dial or programmable feature keys.
It is possible to install more than one KEM depending on the exact model of your IP Phone. Refer to the table below:  
|  **Model**  |  **Number****of KEMs**  |  
| --- | --- |  
|  Cisco IP Phone 8861, 8865, and 8865NR  |  3; providing 108 lines or buttons  |  
|  Cisco IP Phone 8851 and 8851NR  |  2; providing 72 lines or buttons  |  
This article aims to show you how to install a KEM on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones.
## Applicable Devices
  * IP Phone 8800 Series


## Software Version
  * 11.0.1


## Install a Key Expansion Module
### Install a Single Key Expansion Module
Step 1. Disconnect the Ethernet cable from the phone.
Step 2. (Optional) Remove the footstand from the phone.
Step 3. Remove the two accessory connector covers to uncover the slots for the KEM on the right side of the phone, and on the left side of the KEM.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Connect one end of the spine connector to the phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** Ensure that the spine connector is connected to the phone securely.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step4b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step4b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Connect the other end of the spine connector to the KEM.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 6. Fasten the screws into the slots provided at the phone and the KEM.
Step 7. (Optional) Install the footstand on the phone and on the KEM.
Step 8. Connect the Ethernet cable back into the phone.
You now have connected a KEM to your IP phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step8.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installexpmod-step8.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
### Install Multiple Key Expansion Modules
Step 1. Disconnect the Ethernet cable from the phone.
Step 2. (Optional) Remove the footstand from the phone.
Step 3. Remove the two accessory connector covers to uncover the slots for the KEM on the right side of the first KEM, and on the left side of the second KEM.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Connect one end of the spine connector to the first KEM.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** Ensure that it is connected to the first KEM securely.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step4b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step4b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Connect the other end of the spine connector to the second KEM.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-10262017-installmulti-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/picturehere.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** Ensure that it is connected to the KEM securely.
Step 6. Repeat steps 4 and 5 to connect a third KEM.
Step 7. Fasten the screws into the added KEMs.
Step 8. (Optional) Attach the footstands for the phone and the KEMs.
Step 9. Connect the Ethernet cable back into the phone.
You now have connected multiple KEMs to your IP phone.

Connect the Cisco IP Phone 8861 to a Wireless Network
## Objective
The Cisco Internet Protocol (IP) Phone 8861 is equipped with a wireless feature that allows a user to stay connected anywhere in the vicinity of the network. The 8861 provides you the option to connect to a visible or hidden wireless networks. One benefit of having a hidden network is that it reduces the chances of being found by users and attempting to join the network.
The objective of this document is to show you how to connect to a Wireless Local Area Network on a Cisco IP Phone 8861.
**Note:** To use the phone in a Wi-Fi network, you must use a power adaptor to power the phone.
## Applicable Devices
  * CP-8861


## Software Version
  * 11.0


## Connect to a Wireless Network
Connect to a Broadcasted Network
Step 1. If the phone is wired, unplug the Ethernet cable and plug in the power adaptor.
Step 2. On the Cisco IP Phone, press the gear button to access the Information and settings menu.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-202.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-202.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. In the Information and settings menu, navigate to Network Configuration by using the circle navigation button [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-203a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-203a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") and press **Select**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-203b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-203b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. In the Network configuration menu, navigate to Wi-Fi configuration and press **Select**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-204.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-204.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
The phone conducts a wireless scanning process to search for networks in the area.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-204b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-204b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Choose the applicable Service Set Identifier (SSID) of the network. Press the center navigation key to select. If you want to connect to a hidden SSID network, skip to the [Connect to a Hidden Network](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/smb5650-connect-the-cisco-ip-phone-8861-to-a-wireless-network.html#Connect2hidden) section.
**Note:** In this example, the SSID chosen is Cisco-Wireless-5GHz.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-205.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-205.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 6. (Optional) In the Configuration menu of the SSID, which in this case is Cisco-Wireless-5Ghz, choose the mode in which the network uses to encrypt passwords and authenticate clients.
**Note:** In this example, PSK is chosen and only because it is the only option available in the chosen network.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-206.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-206.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 7. Enter the passphrase or password of the chosen network in the _Passphrase_ field.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-207.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-207.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 8. (Optional) Choose an 802.11 mode by pressing the navigation [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-208a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-208a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button. The options are:
  * Auto — IP Phone will scan both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz channels and attempt to associate to the access point with the strongest signal.
  * 2.4 GHz — IP Phone will scan only for 2.4 GHz channels and display 2.4 GHz channels after associating.
  * 5 GHz — IP Phone will scan only for 5 GHz channels and display 5 GHz channels.


**Note:** In this example, 5 Ghz is chosen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-208b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-208b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 9. Press **Connect**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-209.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-209.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 10. A message will appear to inform you that you have successfully connected to the wireless network. Press OK to return to the Network configuration menu.
**Note:** If your phone was previously connected to a wireless network, it will disassociate from the SSID and the phone will reboot.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-2010.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-07122017-step-2010.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Connect to a Hidden Network
Step 1. In the Connect to Wi-Fi menu, choose **Other** to connect to a hidden SSID network.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-201.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-201.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Choose the appropriate Security mode of the SSID network. A list of security modes appear. Below is a list of the available security modes supported and the key management and encryption types that can be used for each mode.
  * EAP-FAST — Extensible Authentication Protocol-Flexible Authentication via Secure Tunneling (EAP-FAST) is an authentication framework rather than a specific authentication mechanism. You will be required to enter a User ID and Password.
  * PEAP-GTC — Protected Extensible Authentication Protocol-Generic Token Card (PEAP-GTC) is a Cisco proprietary method as a substitute to PEAP-MSCHAPv2. You will be required to enter a User ID and Password.
  * PEAP-MSCHAPv2 — Protected Extensible Authentication Protocol-Microsoft Challenge Handshake Authentication Protocol version 2 (PEAP-MSCHAPv2) is a protocol that encapsulates the EAP within an encrypted Transport Layer Security (TLS) tunnel. You will be required to enter a User ID and Password.
  * WEP — Wired Equivalent Privacy security mode requires that the static WEP key (password) must be entered. This option is the least secure.
  * PSK — Pre-shared Key must be configured. Enter a hexadecimal formatted password.
  * None — Choose this security mode if the network does not have security measures enforced.


**Note:** In this example, PSK is chosen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-202.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-202.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Press **Select**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-203.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-203.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Enter the name of the SSID network in the _Network name (SSID)_ field.
**Note:** In this example, Morty is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-204.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-204.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Enter the passphrase or password of the chosen network in the _Passphrase_ field.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-205.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-205.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 6. (Optional) Choose an 802.11 mode by pressing the navigation [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-206a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-206a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button. The options are:
  * Auto — IP Phone will scan both 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz channels and attempt to associate to the access point with the strongest signal.
  * 2.4 GHz — IP Phone will scan only for 2.4 GHz channels and display 2.4 GHz channels after associating.
  * 5 GHz — IP Phone will scan only for 5 GHz channels and display 5 GHz channels.


**Note:** In this example, Auto is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-206b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-206b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 7. Press **Connect**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-207.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-207.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 8. A message will appear to inform you that you have successfully connected to the wireless network. Press OK to return to the Network configuration menu.
**Note:** If your phone was previously connected to a wireless network, it will disassociate from the SSID and the phone will initialize and reboot.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-208.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/ab-connect-20to-20a-20wireless-20network-20on-20the-208861-hidden-07122017-step-208.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")

#### Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. From the list on left, please choose whether this site may use Performance and/or Targeting Cookies. By selecting Strictly Necessary Cookies only, you are requesting Cisco not to sell or share your personal data. Note, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience on the site and the services we are able to offer.
#### Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
Cookies Details
#### Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
These cookies provide metrics related to the performance and usability of our site. They are primarily focused on gathering information about how you interact with our site, including: page load times, response times, error messages, and allowing a replay of a visitor’s interactions with our site, which enables us to review and analyze visitor behavior, helping to improve site usability and functionality. These cookies also allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site and will not be able to monitor its performance.
Cookies Details
#### Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
Cookies Details
#### Functional Cookies
Functional Cookies
These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

## Objective
The objective of this article is to go over the day zero setup of the Cisco Video Phone 8875.
## Applicable Devices | Software
  * Cisco Video Phone 8875 | 1.0 [(Download latest)](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/286331336/type)


### Introduction
Cisco Video Phone 8875 is a video phone with a high-definition camera, a touch screen, and is designed for video calls and meetings in work offices and home offices.
Cisco Video Phone 8875 integration with Webex enables users to join Webex meetings with one button. You do not have to worry about entering meeting IDs and passcodes, save time and join the meeting instantly.
The out of box setup for the 8875 phone happens automatically. To know more, check out the next section.
## Day Zero Setup
#### Step 1
Power on the new Cisco video phone 8875. Click **Start**.
[![Power on the new Cisco video phone 8875.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image1.png "Power on the new Cisco video phone 8875.") [![Click Start.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image2.png "Click Start.")
#### Step 2
It boots the Operating System and detects the network.
[![It boots the Operating System and detects the network.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image3.png "It boots the Operating System and detects the network.")
#### Step 3
If the phone is successfully connected to the Ethernet, it will get an IP address.
[![If the phone is successfully connected to the Ethernet, it will get an IP address.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image4.png "If the phone is successfully connected to the Ethernet, it will get an IP address.")
#### Step 4
If the phone failed to connect to the Ethernet, click on **Network connection**.
[![If the phone failed to connect to the Ethernet, click on Network connection.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image5.png "If the phone failed to connect to the Ethernet, click on Network connection.")
#### Step 5
You will be prompted to unplug the network cable to enable Wi-Fi option.
[![You will be prompted to unplug the network cable to enable Wi-Fi option.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image6.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image6.png "You will be prompted to unplug the network cable to enable Wi-Fi option.")
#### Step 6
To connect to Wi-Fi, select your network from the list.
[![To connect to Wi-Fi, select your network from the list.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image7.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image7.png "To connect to Wi-Fi, select your network from the list.")
#### Step 7
Enter the **Password** and click **Apply**.
[![Enter the Password and click Apply.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image8.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image8.png "Enter the Password and click Apply.")
#### Step 8
Once you are successfully connected to Wi-Fi, click **Next**.
[![Once you are successfully connected to Wi-Fi, click Next.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image9.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image9.png "Once you are successfully connected to Wi-Fi, click Next.")
#### Step 9
The phone will check for the configuration to download. Skip to [Step 12](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875.html#Step12).
[![The phone will check for the configuration to download.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image10.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image10.png "The phone will check for the configuration to download.")
The phone will check in with Cisco’s Enablement Data Orchestration System (EDOS)/Customer Device Activation (CDA) servers to see if there is a record of its MAC address. If it exists, the configuration will be downloaded.
#### Step 10
If you need an activation key to register the phone with Webex Calling, enter the code and click **Activate**. The phone will then connect to the Webex Calling Servers and register itself.
[![If you need an activation key to register the phone with Webex Calling, enter the code and click Activate.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image11.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image11.png "If you need an activation key to register the phone with Webex Calling, enter the code and click Activate.")
You or your administrator need to create the activation code in Webex Calling by signing into your [Webex Control Hub](https://admin.Webex.com) account.
The Settings hard key will be disabled at this stage and will not function until the configuration is applied. If you need to configure your network connection, click on the _Network connection_ button.
#### Step 11
You will see a notification once the activation process is completed successfully.
[![You will see a notification once the activation process is completed successfully.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image12.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image12.png "You will see a notification once the activation process is completed successfully.")
If the code in invalid, you will see an error message as shown below. Enter the correct code or contact your administrator for further assistance.
[![If the code in invalid, you will see an error message.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image13.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image13.png "If the code in invalid, you will see an error message.")
#### Step 12
The configuration will then be applied.
[![The configuration will then be applied.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image14.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3450-day-zero-setup-cp-8875-image14.png "The configuration will then be applied.")
## Conclusion
The out of box setup of the Cisco Video Phone 8875 is as simple as that and you can now use your gear for quality communication.

## Introduction
This document describes how to delete the local password on an MPP phone.  
  

## Prerequisites
### Requirements
This document is not restricted to specific Multiplatform software and hardware versions.
## How to Delete the Local Password on an MPP Device
When you have a brand new MPP phone and you plug it for the first time, it prompts you for a user password. This can be skipped or you can set it.  
  
You can also set or change the user password from the phone screen menu: **Applications** >**Device administration** > **Set password**.  
  
The user password is locally saved to the phone and Cisco does not handle it. This password allows you to set or change the password for access the phone web interfaces and the menus (such as Recent calls, Speed dials, User Preferences and Network configurations.) on the phone screen.   
  
You can notice that a local password was set in the phone if you see a padlock on the upper right corner.
[![Local Password enabled](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8800-series-multiplatform-firmware/220134-delete-user-password-saved-in-mpp-device-00.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8800-series-multiplatform-firmware/220134-delete-user-password-saved-in-mpp-device-00.png "Local Password enabled")
## User Password Menu in Control Hub
If the phone is assigned to a user in Control Hub, you can disable the password by going to **Devices > Select the device > Device Settings. **Scroll down and find **Show User Password Menu**. Disable the toggle, then Save the changes. 
[![Show User Password Menu](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8800-series-multiplatform-firmware/220134-delete-user-password-saved-in-mpp-device-01.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8800-series-multiplatform-firmware/220134-delete-user-password-saved-in-mpp-device-01.png "Show User Password Menu")
After saving the changes go back to the Device, select **Actions** and **Apply Settings.**
**[![Apply Changes](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8800-series-multiplatform-firmware/220134-delete-user-password-saved-in-mpp-device-02.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8800-series-multiplatform-firmware/220134-delete-user-password-saved-in-mpp-device-02.png "Apply Changes")Apply Changes**
If you dont have a way to access to Control Hub to disable User Password Menu and you don`t know the User Password you must apply a [factory reset.](https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/708ce3/Factory-reset-your-Webex-Calling-Multi-Platform-Phones "factory reset")
If the phone is assigned to a user in Control Hub, after the factory reset it must try to register back again to Webex Calling. If the phone does not register back again please contact the Cisco Webex Calling TAC team.
## Related Information
  * [Factory reset your Webex Calling Multi Platform Phones](https://help.webex.com/en-us/article/708ce3/Factory-reset-your-Webex-Calling-Multi-Platform-Phones#id_130156)

## Introduction
This document describes the procedure to set the log level to Debug in MPP (Multiplatform Firmware) Phones from Control Hub.
## Prerequisites
### Requirements
Cisco recommends that you have knowledge of these topics:
  * Webex Calling
  * Control Hub


### Components Used
The information in this document is based on these software versions:
  * Cisco 8851 IP Phone - MPP Firmware 11.3.7


The information in this document was created from the devices in a specific lab environment. All of the devices used in this document started with a cleared (default) configuration. If your network is live, ensure that you understand the potential impact of any command.
## Background Information
When an MPP Phone has a problem or error, the log level must be set in Debug before a PRT (Problem Report Tool) is retrieved from the device to troubleshoot.
## Set the log level
In order to correctly configure the log level, navigate to **Control Hub** > **Devices** and select the device that has the issue. Confirm that the device shows **Online** :
[![Webex Control Hub - Screen Shot 2022-08-17 at 15.38.59](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-00.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-00.png "Webex Control Hub - Screen Shot 2022-08-17 at 15.38.59")
On the Device Page, navigate to the **Device Management** section and select **Device Settings.**
[![Device Management - Screen Shot 2022-08-17 at 15.45.49](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-01.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-01.png "Device Management - Screen Shot 2022-08-17 at 15.45.49")
On **Device Settings** , confirm that **Default Logging Level** is set to **Debugging** and select **Save.**
[![Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 19.59.52](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-02.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-02.png "Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 19.59.52")
**Note** : In order for the changes to take place, reset the device so that it downloads the updated configuration file.
## Generate the PRT
Once the correct log level has been configured in the device, allow time for the problem to occur and generate the PRT.
### Generate the PRT from the Device
**Step 1.** On the device, press the **Applications** button [![ab-gtk-208800-06232017-88xx-front](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-03.jpeg)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-03.jpeg "ab-gtk-208800-06232017-88xx-front") .
**Step 2.** Go to **Status** > **Report Problem.**
**Step 3.** Enter Date and Time of the problem.
**Step 4.** Select a Description from the list.
**Step 5.** Press **Submit.**
### Generate the PRT from Control Hub
**Step 1.** Navigate to **Control Hub** > **Devices** and select the device:
[![Webex Control Hub - Screen Shot 2022-08-17 at 15.38.59](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-04.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-04.png "Webex Control Hub - Screen Shot 2022-08-17 at 15.38.59")
**Step 2.** On the Phone page go to **Support** > **Device Logs.**
[![Device Management - Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 21.07.22](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-05.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-05.png "Device Management - Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 21.07.22")
**Step 3.** On the **Manage Logs** page, select **Generate Log.**
[![Manage Logs - Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 21.16.01](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-06.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-06.png "Manage Logs - Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 21.16.01")
## Verify
Once the PRT has been submitted either manually or via Control Hub, the available logs are listed on the **Manage Logs** section:
[![Manage Logs - Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 21.19.09](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-07.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/collaboration-endpoints/ip-phone-8851/218093-configure-debug-level-in-mpp-phones-regi-07.png "Manage Logs - Screen Shot 2022-08-21 at 21.19.09")

### Bias-Free Language
The documentation set for this product strives to use bias-free language. For the purposes of this documentation set, bias-free is defined as language that does not imply discrimination based on age, disability, gender, racial identity, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, and intersectionality. Exceptions may be present in the documentation due to language that is hardcoded in the user interfaces of the product software, language used based on RFP documentation, or language that is used by a referenced third-party product. [Learn more](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/about/purpose/social-impact/inclusive-language-policy.html) about how Cisco is using Inclusive Language.
## Objective
Blocking anonymous calls on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone lets you filter incoming calls that do not show caller information. If enabled, this feature automatically rejects specific calls.
This article aims to show you how to enable anonymous call blocking on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform through its web-based utility and phone GUI.
### Applicable Devices | Firmware Version
  * IP Phone 8800 Series | 11.0.1 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/284729655))


The 8800 series phones referenced in this article are not Enterprise phones that use a specific call controller. If you would like to compare the two different types of phones, check out [Compare & Contrast: Cisco IP MPP Phones & Cisco Unified IP Phones](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/1574-Compare-and-Contrast-Cisco-IP-MPP-Phones-and-Cisco-Unified-IP-Phones.html). 
## Block Anonymous Call
### Through the Web-based Utility
Step 1. Log in to the web-based utility of the IP phone and click **Admin Login > a****dvanced**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Click **Voice > User**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Under Supplementary Services, choose **Yes** from the Block ANC Setting drop-down menu.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Click **Submit All Changes**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockaweb-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully blocked anonymous calls on your phone through the web-based utility.
### Through the Phone GUI
Step 1. Press the **Applications** button on the IP Phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button, navigate to **User****preferences** then press the**Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Choose **Call preferences** then press the**Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Navigate to **Block a****nonymous****call** and then press the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") right button to set it to**On**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step4b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step4b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Press the **Set** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08312017-blockgui-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You have now enabled anonymous call blocking on your phone through the GUI.

Bias-Free Language
### Bias-Free Language
The documentation set for this product strives to use bias-free language. For the purposes of this documentation set, bias-free is defined as language that does not imply discrimination based on age, disability, gender, racial identity, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, and intersectionality. ## Objective
The Cisco IP Phone 7800 and 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones comprise a set of full-featured Voice-over-Internet Protocol (VoIP) phones that provide voice communication over an IP network. The phones provide all the features of traditional business phones, such as call forwarding, redialing, speed dialing, transferring calls, and conference calling. The Cisco IP Phone 7800 and 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones are targeted for solutions that are centered on third-party Session Initiation Protocol (SIP)-based IP Private Branch Exchange (PBX).
The Cisco IP Phone 7800 and 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones allows you to customize settings such as the phone name, wallpaper, logo, screen saver, brightness display, back light setting, and so on.
This article provides instructions on how to configure the brightness display settings through the web-based utility or the Graphical User Interface (GUI) of your Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone.
### Applicable Devices | Firmware Version
  * IP Phone 7800 Series | 11.0.1 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/284883944))
  * IP Phone 8800 Series | 11.0.1 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/284729655))


## Configure Brightness Display Settings
### Through the Web-based Utility
Step 1. Access the web-based utility of your IP Phone then choose **Admin Login > Advanced**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Choose **Voice > Phone**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Scroll down to the Screen area, then enter a value from 1 to 15 in the _Display Brightness_ field. The higher the number, the greater the brightness on the IP phone screen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** In this example, 15 is used.
Step 4. Click **Submit All Changes**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-web-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully configured the brightness display settings on your Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone through the web-based utility.
### Through the GUI of the IP Phone
Step 1. Press the **Settings** button on your IP Phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Choose **User preferences** using the circle navigation [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step2a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step2a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Choose **Screen preferences**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Select **Display Brightness**. 
Step 5. Press the left or right arrows of the navigation button on your IP Phone to adjust the brightness display.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step4a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step4a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** ​In this example, the display brightness is set to 20. Some models my show a brightness display instead of entering a number. The GUI will adjust the brightness display accordingly.
Step 5. Press the **Set** or **Save** softkey to save the settings.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ijgm-05232017-brightness-display-settings-gui-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully configured the brightness display settings on your Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone through the GUI.

Bias-Free Language
### Bias-Free Language
The documentation set for this product strives to use bias-free language. For the purposes of this documentation set, bias-free is defined as language that does not imply discrimination based on age, disability, gender, racial identity, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, and intersectionality. Exceptions may be present in the documentation due to language that is hardcoded in the user interfaces of the product software, language used based on RFP documentation, or language that is used by a referenced third-party product. [Learn more](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/about/purpose/social-impact/inclusive-language-policy.html) about how Cisco is using Inclusive Language.
## Objective
The Do Not Disturb (DND) feature allows you to bar incoming calls whenever you are on a meeting or on another call. On DND mode, incoming calls may be redirected to another number, the voice mailbox, or disconnected, depending on the call controller you use. 
This article aims to show you some possible ways to enable or disable DND.
### Applicable Devices | Firmware Version
  * IP Phone 7800 Series | 11.0.1 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/284883944))
  * IP Phone 8800 Series | 11.0.1 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/284729655))


## Phones with Multiplatform Firmware
The phones referenced in this article are not Enterprise phones that use a specific call controller. If you would like to compare the two different types of phones, check out [Compare & Contrast: Cisco IP MPP Phones & Cisco Unified IP Phones](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/1574-Compare-and-Contrast-Cisco-IP-MPP-Phones-and-Cisco-Unified-IP-Phones.html "This article will explain the similarities and differences between Cisco Multi-platform Phones \(MPP\), which are made for small to medium size businesses, and Cisco Unified IP Phones, that are made for Enterprise \(large\) businesses.").
MPP phones require either service from an Internet Telephony Service Provider (ITSP) or an IP Private Branch Exchange (PBX) call control server. WebEx Calling, Ring Central, and Verizon are examples of an ITSP. Some examples of IP PBX services that work with Cisco MPP phones include, Asterisk, Centile, and Metaswitch platforms.
These ITSP and IP PBX call controllers are a separate system in which the phone and the call controller communicate with each other to provide services such as call park and voicemail. Since the MPP phones do not use a specific call controller, access and procedures vary. 
Each call controller can follow different procedures, so we can't tell you exactly how yours will work. For information and help with your specific voicemail commands, refer to the help sites from the provider you chose. If you have an administrator, you can contact them for details and possible training.
## Possible Asterisk Commands
In Asterisk, Do Not Disturb is usually controlled by dialing 78 to turn on the Do Not Disturb mode on the phone. To turn the Do Not Disturb mode off, 79 is usually the default. 
## Through the Web-based Utility
Step 1. Access the web-based utility of your IP Phone then choose **Admin Login > advanced**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndweb-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndweb-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Choose **Voice > Phone.**
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndweb-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndweb-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Under Supplementary Services, choose **Yes** from the DND Serv drop-down list to enable DND, or No to disable DND.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-203-1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-203-1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** In this example, Yes is chosen.
Step 4. Click **Submit All Changes**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndweb-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndweb-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have configured DND through the web-based utility of the phone.
## Through the GUI of the Phone
Step 1. Press the **Settings** button on the phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndgui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndgui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Choose **User Preferences** using the Navigation Cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndgui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndgui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-202b-1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-202b-1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Choose **Call Preferences**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-203b-1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-203b-1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Choose **Do not disturb**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-204b-1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-204b-1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Press the left or right arrows of the Navigation Cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndgui-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndgui-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button to enable or disable DND.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-205b-1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-205b-1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** In this example, **On** is chosen.
Step 6. Press the **Set** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-206b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-206b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have configured DND through the GUI of the phone.
### Through the Home Page of the Phone
Step 1. Press the Navigation Cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndhp-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-dndhp-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button until the DND softkey is displayed.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-201c.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-201c.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Press the **DND** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-202c.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/el-083117-configure-20dnd-step-202c.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully configured DND through the home page of your phone.

#### Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. From the list on left, please choose whether this site may use Performance and/or Targeting Cookies. By selecting Strictly Necessary Cookies only, you are requesting Cisco not to sell or share your personal data. Note, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience on the site and the services we are able to offer.
#### Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
Cookies Details
#### Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
These cookies provide metrics related to the performance and usability of our site. They are primarily focused on gathering information about how you interact with our site, including: page load times, response times, error messages, and allowing a replay of a visitor’s interactions with our site, which enables us to review and analyze visitor behavior, helping to improve site usability and functionality. These cookies also allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site and will not be able to monitor its performance.
Cookies Details
#### Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
Cookies Details
#### Functional Cookies
Functional Cookies
These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Bias-Free Language
### Bias-Free Language
The documentation set for this product strives to use bias-free language. For the purposes of this documentation set, bias-free is defined as language that does not imply discrimination based on age, disability, gender, racial identity, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, and intersectionality. Exceptions may be present in the documentation due to language that is hardcoded in the user interfaces of the product software, language used based on RFP documentation, or language that is used by a referenced third-party product. [Learn more](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/about/purpose/social-impact/inclusive-language-policy.html) about how Cisco is using Inclusive Language.
Set Language on a Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone
## Objective
This article aims to show you how to set your preferred language on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform through its web-based utility and phone GUI.
### Applicable Devices | Firmware Version
  * 8800 Series | 11.0.1 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/286311381))


## Set Language - Through the Web-based Utility
Step 1. Log in to the web-based utility of the IP phone and click **Admin Login > a****dvanced**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Click **Voice > ****Regional**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Enter the language you prefer in the _Language Selection_ field under the Language area.
**Note:** In this example, English is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Click **Submit All Changes**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguageweb-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully set the language on your phone through the web-based utility.
## Set Language - Through the Phone GUI
Step 1. Press the **Applications** button on the IP Phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button, navigate to **Device a****dministration** then press the**Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Navigate to **Language** and then press the **Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Choose the language and then press the **Save** softkey.
**Note:** In this example, English-US is chosen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08142017-setlanguagewgui-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully set the language on your phone through the GUI.

Assign a Softkey on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones
## Objective
The Programmable Softkey (PSK) feature allows you to customize the softkeys displayed on your Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones. They can be added, moved and removed, depending on the state of the device. The feature can be enabled or disabled in the web-based utility of the phone.
This article aims to show you how to assign a softkey on your Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones. 
### Applicable Devices | Firmware Version
  * IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones| 11.0 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/284729655))


## Assign a Softkey
### Enable Programmable Softkey
Step 1. Log in to the web-based utility of the IP phone.
Step 2. Click **Admin Login > Advanced**.  
  
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Click **Voice > Phone**.  
  
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Scroll down to the Programmable Softkeys area.
Step 5. From Programmable Softkey Enable drop-down menu, choose **Yes**.  
  
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 6. Choose a programmable softkey number field on which to configure a phone feature.
**Note:** In this example, PSK1 will be edited.  
  
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-6.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-6.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 7. In the _PSK1_ field, enter the string for the programmable softkey in the following format:
fnc=sd;ext=extensionname/starcode@$PROXY;nme=name
**Note:** In this example, the format used is for speed dialing.
Where:
  * fnc= function of the key
  * extensionname=extension being dialed or the star code action to perform
  * name=the name of the speed dial being configured


**Note:** In this example, fnc=sd;ext=6006@$PROXY;nme=6006 is the value entered.  
  
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-7.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-7.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 8. Edit the _Idle Key List_ field to correspond to the new PSK list.
**Note:** In this example, psk1;psk2;psk3;psk4;psk5;psk6 is the value entered.  
  
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-8.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-8.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 9. Click **Submit All Changes**.  
  
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-9.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/el-012317-assign-a-softkey-step-9.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully assigned a softkey on your Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones.
