## Objective
This article aims to show you how to add, edit, or remove a contact from the Personal Directory on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform through its web-based utility and phone GUI.
## Applicable Devices
  * 8800 Series


## Software Version
  * 11.0.1


## Manage Contacts for your Personal Directory
### Through the Web-based Utility
**Add a Contact**
Step 1. Log in to the web-based utility of the IP phone and click **Personal Directory**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Click the **Add to Personal Directory** button.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. In the Add to Personal Directory pop-up window, enter the name of the contact in the _Name_ field. 
**Note:** In this example, Amelia is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. In the _Work Number_ field, enter the work phone number of the contact you wish to add.
**Note:** In this example, 8424 is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. In the _Mobile_ _Number_ field, enter the mobile phone number of the contact you wish to add.
**Note:** In this example, 09240123456 is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 6. In the _Home_ _Number_ field, enter the mobile phone number of the contact you wish to add.
**Note:** In this example, 9221234 is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step6.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step6.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 7. Click **Submit All Changes**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step7.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step7.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have added a contact on your Personal Directory through the phone web-based utility.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step7b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addweb-step7b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Edit a Contact**
Step 1. In the Personal Directory, choose a contact on the list and click the **Edit** button.
**Note:** In this example, the first contact Amelia is chosen to be edited.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editweb-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editweb-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Edit any of the information of the contact then click **Submit All Changes**.
**Note:** In this example, the name Amelia is edited and is changed into Amy.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editweb-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editweb-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully edited a contact on your Personal Directory.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editweb-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editweb-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Remove a Contact**
Step 1. In the Personal Directory, choose a contact on the list by checking the box.
**Note:** In this example, the first contact Amelia is chosen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removeweb-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removeweb-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Click the **Delete Contact** button.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removeweb-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removeweb-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully removed a contact on your Personal Directory.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removeweb-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removeweb-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
### Through the Phone GUI
**Add a Contact**
Step 1. Press the **Directories** button on the IP Phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button, navigate to **Personal address book** then press the **Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Press the **Add** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. In the _Name_ field, enter the name of the contact you wish to add using the number pad on the IP Phone. To do this you use the phone key pad. Find the first letter that you want to enter. You will notice that there is more than one letter per button. The key that contains the letter or number you want can be repeatedly pressed until the letter or number you want is highlighted. Pause when you have the correct one highlighted and that letter or number will be added to the name line. You can then proceed with the rest of the characters. This image shows what appears on the phone screen when the 2 is clicked on the phone three times. 
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/smb5711-manage-contacts-for-your-personal-directory-on-a-cisco-ip-phone-nov-2019-edit-image-1.jpg)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/smb5711-manage-contacts-for-your-personal-directory-on-a-cisco-ip-phone-nov-2019-edit-image-1.jpg "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
In this example, clementine is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button, navigate to the _Work_ field and enter the work phone number of the contact you wish to add.
**Note:** In this example, 5254 is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step5b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step5b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 6. In the _Mobile_ field, enter the mobile phone number of the contact you wish to add.
**Note:** In this example, 09001234567 is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step6.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step6.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 7. In the _Home_ field, enter the mobile phone number of the contact you wish to add.
**Note:** In this example, 2990987 is used.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step7.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step7.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 8. (Optional) Navigate to **Ringtone** and use the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step8.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step8.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button to assign a specific ringtone for this contact.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step8b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step8b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 9. (Optional) Choose a ringtone from the list and press the **Play** softkey if you want to listen to the ringtone first. Otherwise, press **Select**.
**Note:** In this example, Delight is chosen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step9.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step9.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 10. Press the **Save** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step9b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step9b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully added a contact on your Personal address book through the GUI.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step9c.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-addwgui-step9c.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Edit a Contact**
Step 1. In the Personal address book, choose the contact that you wish to edit using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") up or down button and then press **Select** at the center of the Navigation cluster button.
**Note:** In this example, the first contact Amelia is chosen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step1a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step1a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Edit any of the information that you wish to modify and then press the **Save** softkey.
**Note:** In this example, the Work phone number is edited and changed to 5421.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully edited a contact on your Personal address book.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-editwgui-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Remove a Contact**
Step 1. In the Personal address book, choose the contact that you wish to remove using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") up or down button and then press the **Option** softkey.
**Note:** In this example, the first contact Amelia is chosen.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step1b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step1b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button, navigate to **Delete** and then press the **Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Press the **OK** softkey when prompted.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully removed a contact on your Personal address book.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step3b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-08302017-removewgui-step3b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")

Configure TR-069 on the Cisco IP Phone 7800 Series or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone
## Objective
TR-069 defines the Customer Premise Equipment Wide Area Network Management Protocol (CWMP). It describes the interaction between an auto-configuration server (ACS) and one or more endpoints that supports CWMP. TR-069 makes “no-touch” installation, deployment of new services, firmware maintenance, and troubleshooting possible. Configuring TR-069 on the Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phones allows the device to communicate with the ACS and be able to request updates. It will also allow the ACS to instantly reach the phone in case new services are to be deployed.
This article aims to show you how to configure TR-069 on the Cisco IP Phone 7800 Series or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone. It assumes that the TR-069 settings on the ACS has already been configured. To complete the configuration, the following details are needed:
  * ACS Username
  * ACS Password
  * ACS URL
  * Connection Request Username
  * Connection Request Password
  * (Optional) Backup ACS URL
  * (Optional) Backup ACS Username
  * (Optional) Backup ACS Password


## Applicable Devices
  * 7800 Series
  * 8800 Series


## Software Version
  * 11.0.1


## Configure TR-069
Step 1. Log in to the web-based utility of the phone and click **Admin Login > a****dvanced**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Click the **Voice** tab.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Click the **TR-069** sub-tab.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Under TR-069, choose **Yes** from the Enable TR-069 drop-down list.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is No. In this example, Yes is chosen.
Step 5. Enter the ACS URL in the _ACS URL_ field. The ACS URL is provided by the Internet Service Provider (ISP).
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** In this example, [www.cpeacs.com](http://www.cpeacs.com) is entered.
Step 6. Enter the user name in the _ACS Username_ field. This is the username that would allow the phone to connect to the ACS.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step6.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step6.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** In this example, CPE1 is entered.
Step 7. Enter the password in the _ACS Password_ field. This is the password that would allow the phone to connect to the ACS.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step7.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step7.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 8. Enter the request username in the _Connection Request Username_ field. This will be used by the ACS to authenticate the CPE.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step8.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step8.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** In this example, CPEUser is entered.
Step 9. Enter the request password in the _Connection Request Password_ field. This will be used by the ACS to complete the authentication process with the CPE.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step9.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step9.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 10. (Optional) Enter the inform interval value in the _Periodic Inform Interval_ field. The interval value is measured in seconds. It determines the interval at which the phone contacts to the ACS.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step10.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step10.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is 20. In this example, 20 is used.
Step 11. (Optional) Verify that Periodic Inform Enable is set to Yes. This allows the phone to communicate with the ACS periodically. This can be changed by choosing an option from the Periodic Inform Enable drop-down list.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step11.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step11.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is Yes.
Step 12. (Optional) From the TR-069 Traceability drop-down list, choose **Yes** to activate TR-069 transaction traceability. Choose **No** to disable the feature.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step12.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step12.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is No.
Step 13. (Optional) From the CWMP V1.2 Support drop-down list, choose **Yes** to enable the feature. Choose **No** to deactivate.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step13.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step13.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is Yes.
Step 14. (Optional) From the TR-069 VoiceObject Init drop-down list, choose **Y****es** to activate the feature. Choose **No** to deactivate.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step14.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step14.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is Yes.
Step 15. (Optional) From the TR-069 DHCPOption Init drop-down list, choose **Yes** to activate the feature. Choose **No** to deactivate.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step15.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step15.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is Yes.
Step 16. (Optional) From the TR-069 Fallback Support drop-down list, choose **Yes** to enable the feature. Choose **No** to deactivate.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step16.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step16.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** The default value is No.
Step 17. (Optional) Enter the backup ACS URL in the _BACKUP ACS URL_ field.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step17.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step17.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** By default, this field is left blank.
Step 18. (Optional) Enter the backup ACS username in the _BACKUP ACS User_ field.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step18.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step18.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** By default, this field is left blank.
Step 19. (Optional) Enter the backup ACS password in the _BACKUP ACS Password_ field.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step19.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step19.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** By default, this field is left blank.
Step 20. Click **Submit All Changes**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step20.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step20.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have configured TR-069 on your IP Phone.
### Verify TR-069 is Working
Step 1. Using Wireshark, perform a packet capture on the phone.
**Note:** In this example, the phone is sending an XML file packaged in a Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP).
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step21.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/ell-08112017-tr09-step21.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You have just confirmed that the TR-069 configuration is working.
[![Back to Top](https://www.cisco.com/etc/designs/cdc/fw/i/responsive/Default-bTop-36.svg)Back to Top](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/smb5687-configure-tr-069-on-the-cisco-ip-phone-7800-series-or-8800-s.html "Back to Top")

Secure a Call on a Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone
## Objective
Encrypting calls on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone lets you secure your outbound calls to protect them from eavesdroppers. If this feature is enabled, a lock icon will be displayed on the phone GUI next to the dialed phone number.
This article aims to show you how to secure a call on the Cisco IP Phone 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone.
## Applicable Devices
  * 8800 Series


## Software Version
  * 11.0.1


## Secure a Call
### Through the Web-based Utility
Step 1. Log in to the web-based utility of the IP Phone and click **Admin Login > a****dvanced**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Click **Voice > User**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Under Supplementary Services, choose **Yes** from the Secure Call Setting drop-down menu.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Click **Submit All Changes**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecall-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully enabled Secure Call on your phone through the web-based utility.
### Through the Phone GUI
Step 1. Press the **Applications** button on the IP Phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Using the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button, navigate to **User****preferences** then press the**Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step2b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step2b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Choose **Call preferences** then press the**Select** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Navigate to **Secure****call** and then press the Navigation cluster [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step4.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") right button to set it to**On**.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step4b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step4b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Press the **Set** softkey.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step5.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have enabled Secure call on your phone through the GUI as indicated by the lock icon.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step5b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/rjs-07282017-securecallgui-step5b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")

#### Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. #### Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

#### Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
These cookies provide metrics related to the performance and usability of our site. They are primarily focused on gathering information about how you interact with our site, including: page load times, response times, error messages, and allowing a replay of a visitor’s interactions with our site, which enables us to review and analyze visitor behavior, helping to improve site usability and functionality. These cookies also allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site and will not be able to monitor its performance.

kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875
## Objective
The objective of this article is to briefly go over some of the touch screen display and navigation options in Cisco video phone 8875.
### Applicable Devices | Software Version
  * Cisco Video Phone 8875 | 1.0 [(Download latest)](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/286331336/type)


### Introduction
Cisco Video Phone 8875 is a video phone with a high-definition camera, a touch screen, and is designed for video calls and meetings in work offices and home offices.
Cisco Video Phone 8875 integration with Webex enables users to join Webex meetings with one button. You do not have to worry about entering meeting IDs and passcodes, save time and join the meeting instantly.
Features of the 7-inch touch screen includes: 
  * It has a 1024 × 600 high resolution and provides scrollable access to calling features and text-based XML applications. 
  * You can expand the lines without limitation of hardware keys.
  * It is also easy for search and input based on virtual keyboard support on touch screen.


Keep reading to find out more about the touch screen display and navigation options in the Cisco video phone 8875.
## Touchscreen Display and Navigation
To wake up the phone from sleep mode, you can touch the capacitive touch LED button.
[![To wake up the phone from sleep mode, you can touch the capacitive touch LED button.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image1.png "To wake up the phone from sleep mode, you can touch the capacitive touch LED button.") [![The LED screen will become active.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image2.png "The LED screen will become active.")
To navigate to the menu options, touch any of the icons displayed.
[![To navigate to the menu options, touch any of the icons displayed.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image3.png "To navigate to the menu options, touch any of the icons displayed.")
The two dots at the bottom of the LED screen tells you that there are two pages. Simply swipe to the left or right to navigate between screens.
[![The two dots at the bottom of the LED screen tells you that there are two pages.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image4.png "The two dots at the bottom of the LED screen tells you that there are two pages.")
To access the settings menu, press the [![Settings button.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image5.png "Settings button.") button.
[![To access the settings menu, press the settings button.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image6.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image6.png "To access the settings menu, press the settings button.")
The _Settings_ screen will be displayed. You can now navigate to any of the options by touching the screen.
[![The Settings screen will be displayed. You can now navigate to any of the options by touching the screen.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image7.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image7.png "The Settings screen will be displayed. You can now navigate to any of the options by touching the screen.")
When you scroll up or down the page, the scroll bar becomes visible.
[![When you scroll up or down the page, the scroll bar becomes visible.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image8.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image8.png "When you scroll up or down the page, the scroll bar becomes visible.")
Use the arrow on the upper left corner of the screen to navigate back.
[![Use the arrow on the upper left corner of the screen to navigate back.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image9.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3451-touchscreen-display-and-navigation-cp-8875-image9.png "Use the arrow on the upper left corner of the screen to navigate back.")
## Conclusion
It’s as simple as that! Now you know all about the basic touch screen display and navigation options in Cisco video phone 8875.

#### Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. #### Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.

These cookies provide metrics related to the performance and usability of our site. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.

kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad
## Objective
The objective of this article is to show you how to factory reset the Cisco video phone 8875 using the keypad.
### Applicable Devices
  * Cisco Video Phone 8875


### Introduction
Cisco Video Phone 8875 is a video phone with a high-definition camera, a touch screen, and is designed for video calls and meetings in work offices and home offices.
Cisco Video Phone 8875 integration with Webex enables users to join Webex meetings with one button. You do not have to worry about entering meeting IDs and passcodes, save time and join the meeting instantly.
A factory reset clears all settings from your phone. You lose your current registration and all the configuration after a factory reset. You must register and set up your phone as you do for a new phone before you can use it again.
When you encounter severe technical problems with your phone or you want to clear the existing configuration, a factory reset can help.
Let’s dive into the steps to perform a factory reset of the Cisco video phone 8875 using the keypad.
## Reset your phone with the keypad
#### Step 1
Unplug the phone.
  * If using Power over Ethernet (PoE), unplug the Ethernet cable.
  * If using the power cube, unplug the power cube.


Wait for 5 seconds.
[![Unplug the phone.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image1.png "Unplug the phone.")
#### Step 2
Press and hold **#** key and plug the phone back in.
[![Press and hold # key and plug the phone back in. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image2.png "Press and hold # key and plug the phone back in. ")
#### Step 3
The Headset button, the Speaker button, and the Mute button will be illuminated.
[![The Headset button, the Speaker button and the Mute button will be illuminated. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image3.png "The Headset button, the Speaker button and the Mute button will be illuminated. ")
#### Step 4
When the mute button goes off, release the # button and press **123456789*0#** in sequence. After you press these buttons, the mute LED will be illuminated again, and the phone will go through the factory reset process.
[![When the mute button goes off, release # button and press 123456789*0# in sequence. After you press these buttons, the mute LED will be illuminated again, and the phone will go through the factory reset process. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image4.png "When the mute button goes off, release # button and press 123456789*0# in sequence. After you press these buttons, the mute LED will be illuminated again, and the phone will go through the factory reset process. ")
If you press the buttons out of sequence, the phone powers on normally. Also, the timing of pressing the buttons is important for a successful factory reset.
#### Step 5
Once the factory reset is completed, the phone will go through the out of box workflow.
[![Once the factory reset is completed, the phone will go through the out of box workflow. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3452-factory-reset-cp-8875-using-keypad-image5.png "Once the factory reset is completed, the phone will go through the out of box workflow. ")
## Conclusion
It is as simple as that! Now you know how to factory reset the Cisco video phone 8875 using the keypad.

kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875
## Objective
The objective of this article is to go over the USB ports and their features in Cisco video phone 8875.
### Applicable Devices
  * Cisco Video Phone 8875


### Introduction
Cisco Video Phone 8875 is a video phone with a high-definition camera, a touch screen, and is designed for video calls and meetings in work offices and home offices.
Cisco Video Phone 8875 integration with Webex enables users to join Webex meetings with one button. You do not have to worry about entering meeting IDs and passcodes, save time and join the meeting instantly.
## Table of Contents
  * [USB Ports](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875.html#usb-ports)
  * [USB Charging and Overcurrent Protection](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875.html#usb-charging-and-overcurrent-protection)


## USB Ports
The 8875 phone has two USB ports:
  * A side USB A port
  * A rear USB C port

[![Side USB-A port.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image1.png "Side USB-A port.") [![Rear USB-C port.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image2.png "Rear USB-C port.")
Maximum power draw for each port:
  * Side USB-A: Max Power 2.5W (5v 0.5A) or 10.5W (5V 2.1A)
  * Rear USB-C: Max Power 2.5W (5v 0.5a)


## USB Charging and Overcurrent Protection
With regular charging, type-A and type-C support a maximum current of 0.5A, and USB quick charging supports a maximum current of 2.1A.
If the power required by the powered device is greater than 0.5A and 2.1A, the phone will turn off the USB port to protect itself and prohibit the powered device from charging. It will also display a prompt on the LCD to unplug the powered device. Click **OK** to open the port.
[![USB-A device overcurrent promt.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image3.png "USB-A device overcurrent promt.") [![USB-C device overcurrent promt.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3449-usb-ports-cp-8875-image4.png "USB-C device overcurrent promt.")
## Conclusion
It’s as simple as that! Now you have all the information about the USB ports and their features in Cisco video phone 8875.

## Objective
The objective of this article is to go over the capacitive touch LED feature in Cisco video phone 8875.
### Applicable Devices
  * Cisco Video Phone 8875


### Introduction
Cisco Video Phone 8875 is a video phone with a high-definition camera, a touch screen, and is designed for video calls and meetings in work offices and home offices.
Cisco Video Phone 8875 integration with Webex enables users to join Webex meetings with one button. You do not have to worry about entering meeting IDs and passcodes, save time and join the meeting instantly.
On the front of the 8875 phone there is a capacitive touch LED button that serves several purposes. Keep reading to find out more!
## Table of Contents
  * [Capacitive Touch LED Button](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875.html#capacitive-touch-led-button)
  * [CAP LED Behavior ](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875.html#cap-led-behavior)


## Capacitive Touch LED Button
[![Capacitive Touch LED Button.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image1.png "Capacitive Touch LED Button.")
  * The button itself will wake the phone up from sleep and return your phone to the home screen from wherever it is.
  * It also provides system feedback based off the light level and patterns.


## CAP LED Behavior 
#### Step 1
On the initial power up, as soon as the Cisco Logo is displayed on the screen, the center dot LED and the outer ring LED will turn on with 100% brightness.
[![On the initial power up, as soon as the Cisco Logo is displayed on the screen, the center dot LED and the outer ring LED will turn on with 100% brightness.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image2.png "On the initial power up, as soon as the Cisco Logo is displayed on the screen, the center dot LED and the outer ring LED will turn on with 100% brightness.")
#### Step 2
The Cisco logo will disappear. The LEDs will then turn off and the phone will either begin the Day 0 setup or it will begin registration. The outer ring LED will turn on with 100% brightness with the center dot turned off.
[![The outer ring LED will turn on with 100% brightness with the center dot turned off.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image3.png "The outer ring LED will turn on with 100% brightness with the center dot turned off.")
#### Step 3
Once the boot is complete and the phone has registered successfully, the outer ring LED will dim to only 30% brightness.
[![Once the boot is complete and the phone has registered successfully, the outer ring LED will dim to only 30% brightness.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image4.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image4.png "Once the boot is complete and the phone has registered successfully, the outer ring LED will dim to only 30% brightness.")
If the phone boots and the registration fail, it will turn the both the dot and the ring LED off.
[![If the phone boots and the registration fail, it will turn the both the dot and the ring LED off.](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image5.png "If the phone boots and the registration fail, it will turn the both the dot and the ring LED off.")
#### Step 4
When the screen goes to sleep mode, the backlight timer turns off and the LED will go into a breathing state by changing from 30% brightness to 100% brightness and back.
[![When the screen goes to sleep mode, the backlight timer turns off and the LED will go into a breathing state by changing from 30% brightness to 100% brightness and back. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image6.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image6.png "When the screen goes to sleep mode, the backlight timer turns off and the LED will go into a breathing state by changing from 30% brightness to 100% brightness and back. ")
#### Step 5
You can control the backlight LED time in the Webex Calling control hub or on systems not registered to Webex Calling, navigate to Admin login. Select **Voice > User** menu. Scroll down to the _Screen_ section to configure the _Back Light Timer_.
[![Navigate to Admin login. Select Voice > User menu. Scroll down to the Screen section to configure the Back Light Timer. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image7.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3448-capacitive-touch-led-cp-8875-image7.png "Navigate to Admin login. Select Voice > User menu. Scroll down to the Screen section to configure the Back Light Timer. ")
## Conclusion
There you have it! Now you know all about the capacitive touch LED feature in Cisco video phone 8875.

#### Your Privacy
When you visit any website, it may store or retrieve information on your browser, mostly in the form of cookies. This information might be about you, your preferences or your device and is mostly used to make the site work as you expect it to. The information does not usually directly identify you, but it can give you a more personalized web experience. Because we respect your right to privacy, you can choose not to allow some types of cookies. From the list on left, please choose whether this site may use Performance and/or Targeting Cookies. By selecting Strictly Necessary Cookies only, you are requesting Cisco not to sell or share your personal data. Note, blocking some types of cookies may impact your experience on the site and the services we are able to offer.
#### Strictly Necessary Cookies
Always Active
These cookies are necessary for the website to function and cannot be switched off in our systems. They are usually only set in response to actions made by you which amount to a request for services, such as setting your privacy preferences, logging in or filling in forms. You can set your browser to block or alert you about these cookies, but some parts of the site will not then work. These cookies do not store any personally identifiable information.
Cookies Details
#### Performance Cookies
Performance Cookies
These cookies provide metrics related to the performance and usability of our site. They are primarily focused on gathering information about how you interact with our site, including: page load times, response times, error messages, and allowing a replay of a visitor’s interactions with our site, which enables us to review and analyze visitor behavior, helping to improve site usability and functionality. These cookies also allow us to count visits and traffic sources so we can measure and improve the performance of our site. They help us to know which pages are the most and least popular and see how visitors move around the site. If you do not allow these cookies we will not know when you have visited our site and will not be able to monitor its performance.
Cookies Details
#### Targeting Cookies
Targeting Cookies
These cookies may be set through our site by our advertising partners. They may be used by those companies to build a profile of your interests and show you relevant adverts on other sites. They do not store directly personal information, but are based on uniquely identifying your browser and internet device. If you do not allow these cookies, you will experience less targeted advertising.
Cookies Details
#### Functional Cookies
Functional Cookies
These cookies enable the website to provide enhanced functionality and personalisation. They may be set by us or by third party providers whose services we have added to our pages. If you do not allow these cookies then some or all of these services may not function properly.

Bias-Free Language
### Bias-Free Language
The documentation set for this product strives to use bias-free language. For the purposes of this documentation set, bias-free is defined as language that does not imply discrimination based on age, disability, gender, racial identity, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, and intersectionality. Exceptions may be present in the documentation due to language that is hardcoded in the user interfaces of the product software, language used based on RFP documentation, or language that is used by a referenced third-party product. [Learn more](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/about/purpose/social-impact/inclusive-language-policy.html) about how Cisco is using Inclusive Language.
## Objective
The objective of this article is to get you familiar with the Cisco Video Phone 8875.
### Applicable Devices
  * CP-8875 


### Introduction
Cisco Video Phone 8875 is a video phone with a high definition camera, a touch screen, and is designed for video calls and meetings in work offices and home offices. 
Cisco Video Phone 8875 integration with Webex enables users to join Webex meetings with one button. You do not have to worry about entering meeting IDs and passcodes, save time and join the meeting instantly.
## Hardware Features
[![CP-8875 hardware features. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3447-get-to-know-CP-8875-image1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3447-get-to-know-CP-8875-image1.png "CP-8875 hardware features. ")
  * 7" 1024x600 LCD with Touch
  * 1080p HD Camera, up to 30 fps
  * Wi-Fi 802.11a/b/g/n/ac
  * Bluetooth 4.1 LE
  * Two USB Ports: Type A and Type C
  * 10/100/1000 Switch Port
  * POE Class 4 (802.3at)
  * RJ9, AUX port for EHS
  * Capacitive touch button

[![CP-8875 front view. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3447-get-to-know-CP-8875-image2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3447-get-to-know-CP-8875-image2.png "CP-8875 front view.   1. Handset and Message Waiting Indicator (MWI)

  6. Headset, Speakerphone, and Mute
  7. Alphanumeric Keypad

CP-8875 does not have any line key or soft key buttons.

## Power Button
A new feature in CP-8875 phones is a power button located on the right side of the phone near the bottom. Once the phone is connected to power, press the power button to have the phone enter deep sleep mode. Pressing the power button again will wake the phone up from sleep. It takes approximately a minute for the phone to be ready for use after waking it up from deep sleep mode.
[![CP-8875 power button. ](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3447-get-to-know-CP-8875-image5.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-8800-series/images/kmgmt3447-get-to-know-CP-8875-image5.png "CP-8875 power button. ")

## Introduction
This document describes best practices to clean and troubleshoot Cisco IP Phone Hookswitches in order to prevent unnecessary Return Material Authorizations (RMAs).
## Prerequisites
### Requirements
There are no specific prerequisites for this document.
### Components Used
The information in this document is based on the Cisco 7800 and 8800 series IP Phones.
## Background Information
A thorough analysis of a large number of Cisco IP Phones that have been reported as hardware failures reveals that the great majority of these phones do not have any determinable failure. The standard by which the phone industry measures phone failures is based on Bell Corp/Telcordia standards and the standard acceptable failure rate is set at four percent. The Cisco IP Phone's overall failure rate is well under the acceptable industry average. Many of the problems that have been reported as hardware failures are really either operational or cleanup issues. This document describes some common steps you can take to troubleshoot certain issues before you replace a Cisco IP Phone.
## Clean and Troubleshoot the Cisco IP Phone Hookswitch
This section highlights some guidelines for phone usage and what to look for if you suspect a hookswitch failure.
**Note** : A slightly dampened soft cloth must be used to clean or wipe down the phone. Do not use any liquids or powders directly on the phone to clean or for other purposes. As with all but weatherproof electronics, liquids and powders can contaminate the components and cause failures.
### Signaling
Check to see whether signaling works properly between the phone and the Cisco CallManager. Use the speaker button to answer the phone or take the phone off-hook. If the call is answered or dial tone is received, signaling is active.
### Cradle Clip
The phones are designed with a reversible clip in the handset cradle area. The clip is used with the tab out when the phone is wall-mounted. Check to see whether the cradle handset clip is in the wall-mounted position (with a plastic tab that protrudes upward). If the phone is on a desktop, slide the clip upward to remove it, rotate 180 degrees, and slide back in so that the tab is hidden.
This tab can interfere with the handset as it is replaced on the base (in the cradle), which causes the hookswitch to remain in the up position. When the handset is lifted later in an attempt to initiate a new call or answer one, the hookswitch is not activated. If you answer a call, the phone continues to ring; if you place a call, no dial tone occurs.
### LAN Cord
Check to see whether the dark gray cord / LAN cable that was packaged with the phone is in use. If a different patch cable is in use, position it to pass out the side of the phone, between the base and the footstand. Other cables such as Cat-5, Cat-5E, or Cat-6 that have larger diameters can be too large for the pass-through opening and tilt the phone forward. The footstand is designed to allow the most number of positions to eliminate glare from the display. When the phone is adjusted to the most vertical position, larger diameter cords can force the phone forward to the point where the handset does not sit firmly on the hookswitch. This creates false off-hook conditions.
Keep the phone one notch from the most vertical position to ensure that the handset firmly rests on the hookswitch.
### Self-Clean Hookswitch Contacts
The hookswitch contacts design uses a wipe action to self-clean the contacts. Extended periods of time without use of the phone allow air impurities such as dust and other contaminants to hinder contact performance, which results in intermittent operation. Press and release the hookswitch rapidly a dozen times or so to clean the contacts.
**Note** : If none of these solutions resolve the issue, you can start the RMA process for the phone.

## Introduction
This document describes how to properly clean Cisco IP Phones and provides guidance on the safest way to keep your device clean.
## Background Information
Your safety is a top concern and Cisco understands that the COVID-19 pandemic has had a significant impact to certain industries such as healthcare.
In order to address the needs of these markets and ensure that you and your colleagues stay safe, you must consider the guidelines in this document to clean and disinfect your desk phones.
## General Information
The Cisco desktop IP phone is not fully sealed, the internal electronics on IP phones can be damaged when exposed to water, liquids, or powders.
Please ensure the device is turned off and unplugged to avoid any short circuits or other risks before cleaning.
When you clean a Cisco phone, do not spray any liquid substance directly on the device. Instead, use a damp cloth or wipe to lightly scrub the touchpoints of the phone. If the cloth is wet, the gaps in the plastic on the device can allow liquid to reach the sensitive electronics of the phone. As with all non-weatherproof electronics, liquids and powders can damage the components and cause hardware failures.
To clean the phones, Caviwipes and Saniwipes containing less than 17% isopropanol or approximately 75% ethanol alcohol are recommended. And there are a few important points to remember about cleaning IP phones:
  * Please ensure that no liquid seeps inside the phone, as this may damage the internal electronic components.
  * Do not use harsh chemical agents, such as bleach or other chemicals, to clean the exterior case on a phone.
  * Clean your phone immediately if it comes in contact with anything that could cause stains, or other damage; for example, dirt or sand, ink, makeup, soap, detergent, acids, acidic foods, or lotions.


**Note** : Use of Caviwipes or Saniwipes more than three times a day can damage the exterior surface of a phone and adversely affect the phone's appearance.

Set the Password on the Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone
## Objective
Administrators can let users protect their Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone with a password for added security. This is typically done when the phone is booted for the first time, or after the phone is reset to its factory default settings to prevent unauthorized changes to the settings of the phone. Administrators can also set the password through the Graphical User Interface (GUI) of the phone.
This article aims to show you how to set a password on the Cisco IP Phone 7800 and or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone.
### Applicable Devices | Firmware Version
  * 7800 Series | V 11.0 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/286311381))
  * 8800 Series | V 11.0 ([Download latest](https://software.cisco.com/download/home/286311381))


## Set the Password via the IP Phone GUI
**Note:** When booting up the Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone for the first time, or after resetting the phone, you will be prompted to set up a password. Proceed to [Steps 4 to 6](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/smb5460-set-the-password-on-the-cisco-ip-phone-7800-or-8800-series-m.html#step4).
Step 1. Press the **Setting****s** button on the IP phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-201.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-201.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. Choose **Device a****dministration** using the [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-202a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-202a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") navigation button.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-202b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-202b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. Choose **Set****p****assword** using the [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-203a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-203a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") button.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-203b.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-203b.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 4. Enter the password that you want to use in the _New p_ _assword_ field. The password can be a combination of letters, numbers, and special characters.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-204.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-204.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 5. Re-enter the password in the _Reenter_ _n_ _ew_ _p_ _assword_ field.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-205.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-205.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 6. Press the **Save** softkey to confirm.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-206.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gs-setpwphone-07042017-step-206.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
You should now have successfully set a password on your IP phone through its GUI.

### Bias-Free Language
The documentation set for this product strives to use bias-free language. For the purposes of this documentation set, bias-free is defined as language that does not imply discrimination based on age, disability, gender, racial identity, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic status, and intersectionality. Exceptions may be present in the documentation due to language that is hardcoded in the user interfaces of the product software, language used based on RFP documentation, or language that is used by a referenced third-party product. [Learn more](https://www.cisco.com/site/us/en/about/purpose/social-impact/inclusive-language-policy.html) about how Cisco is using Inclusive Language.
Reset Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone to Default Settings
## Objective
Resetting the Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone to default setting lets you revert all the settings of the phone to factory default settings. This is typically done when the phone needs to be rid of its settings and be configured with a new one. For example, the phone is to be deployed to another user. You can reset the phone to its default settings before putting in new ones to ensure that the configuration from the previous user is removed from the phone.
This article aims to show you how to reset the Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone to default settings.
**Note:** You might also need to perform the reset process through your call manager if you are using one. Check the information about assigning a phone to another user on the documentation of your call manager.
## Applicable Devices
  * 8800 Series
  * 7800 Series


## Reset the IP Phone
**Note:** Before resetting your Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone, ensure the following:
  * The phone should be connected to a Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP)-enabled network.
  * The Trivial File Transfer Protocol (TFTP) server IP address should be configured with option 150 or option 66.


Step 1. Disconnect power from the phone. If you are using Power over Ethernet (PoE) as the power source of the phone, disconnect the Ethernet cable from the phone. If you are using a power adapter, disconnect the power cable.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step1.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step1.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 2. After five seconds, press and hold the **Pound** (#) key and then reconnect power to the phone.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step2.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step2.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
Step 3. As soon as the mute indicator light turns off, release the pound key and then press **1** , **2** , **3** , **4** , **5** , **6** , **7** , **8** , **9** , ***** , **0** , **#** sequentially. You should finish pressing all the mentioned keys in less than five seconds, otherwise, the reset process will not be successful.
[![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step3.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step3.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.")
**Note:** After pressing the keypad, the mute button [![](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step3a.png)](https://www.cisco.com/c/dam/en/us/support/docs/smb/collaboration-endpoints/cisco-ip-phone-7800-series/images/gss-04242017-resetphone-step3a.png "Related image, diagram or screenshot.") will light up to indicate that the reset process has been initiated. Do not disconnect the power from the phone while it is going through the factory reset process.
Step 4. Wait until the light on the mute button will turn off and the phone will start to reboot. Once rebooted, the reset is now done.
You should now have successfully reset your Cisco IP Phone 7800 or 8800 Series Multiplatform Phone to its factory default settings.
